canonical_addressing: Canonical addressing: mandates in this document are cited as `Mandate N` (Pillar I) or `Pillar <N> item N` (Pillars II–IV). Source comments predating this document's current structure used to also cite `Rule N`, `Aspiration N`, and `ENGINE-N` — none of those schemes ever corresponded to this document's current numbering, and no reconciliation table exists. As of 2026-09-18 those stale citations were reconciled across every file that carried them. This happened in two passes, and the first pass's own "zero remain" claim was itself wrong: a case-sensitive sweep found 96 mixed-case `Rule N`/`Aspiration N`/`ENGINE-N` occurrences across 19 files and fixed all of them, but the sweep's own regex only matched `Rule` (not `RULE`), so it silently missed 17 further all-caps `RULE N` occurrences across 10 files — caught and fixed in a second pass once discovered. Combined, every citation was either stripped down to its still-accurate descriptive text (the numbered scheme dropped, the reasoning kept — the large majority) or, in the handful of cases where the reference was verifiably the same concept under a new name, rewritten to its real current citation: `admin.rs`'s and `evolution.rs`'s/`reflex_synth.rs`'s "Motion Rule (Protocol)" citations to `Pillar IV item 3` and `Mandate 20` respectively (two genuinely distinct concepts that historically shared the same name, per Mandate 20's own collision note), and `security.rs`'s/`net_guard.rs`'s exact-title matches to `Mandate 10`/`Mandate 12`. No correspondence was ever invented without a verifiable match — where a plausible-looking old number didn't match a current mandate's substance, the number was dropped rather than guessed. Two test-fixture strings in `amas.rs` containing the literal words "test aspiration 23" (simulated mission-goal text, not code comments) were correctly left untouched by both passes.
citation_drift_note: A related, distinct kind of drift — comments citing `Mandate N` using the *current* terminology with a number that doesn't match this document's actual current mandate at that number — was scoped and fixed separately (`EV-2022920-031`): 5 of 41 such citations were wrong, corrected or stripped the same way.
description:
This ledger defines the engine's constitutional mandates, component
topology, execution model, and release/runtime protocols. It is the source
of truth compiled into the binary at build time (see `susi-gawd-agents build.rs → AlphaSelf`).
The public host contract in `README.md` must stay consistent with this document
and with `susi_paths::ports` / `SusiDaemon` — when they disagree, source wins
and both documents are updated in the same change.

design_principles.summary: Mandates 46 and 62; agents deliver authorized engineering work end-to-end without CEO code review. User authorization, privacy and spend boundaries remain explicit; evidence is required for completion.
design_principles.title: Autonomous by default

design_principles.summary: claims checked against tools and workspace state. Mission finals require live `ToolReceipt` citations or other absolute truth sources (`TruthTransformer`); EpistemicAuditor rejects hallucinated paths and failed `EvidenceRecord` trails.
design_principles.title: Grounded outputs

design_principles.summary: Mandate 26; thinking and tool calls are inspectable. Mission reports expose agent interactions + evidence ledger + blackboard in protocol output and persist `.susi/last_mission_trace.json` / `.susi/last_blackboard.json` (hashes/provenance for tools; no secret bodies — Mandate 38); tool receipts append to the cross-process-serialized, generational `.susi/receipt_archive.jsonl` archive (hashes/provenance only — not truth authority). Not unbounded "100% transparency."
design_principles.title: Traceable reasoning

design_principles.summary: Tokio, Rayon, Crossbeam, parking_lot on real hardware (Mandates 5, 28–30). Swarm dispatch uses Rayon work-stealing; daemon/HTTP use Tokio; pulse queue uses Crossbeam `SegQueue`; shared state prefers `parking_lot` / DashMap — lock-preferring, not a "zero blocking forever" claim.
design_principles.title: Concurrency-first

design_principles.summary: Mandates 43 and 63; Rust-only Susi runtime, tooling and shipped dependency closure are requirements. Existing non-Rust paths are migration defects, not exemptions or evidence of compliance.
design_principles.title: Rust substrate

design_principles.summary: Mandates 44 and 70; normal operation requires no user-written configuration. Native discovery/defaults and agent repair carry the setup burden; credentials and paid-service consent remain explicit.
design_principles.title: Zero-config auto

design_principles.summary: RSI swarm AI OS for hosting, provisioning, and managing any local and cloud AI ecosystem (Mandate 45) — an OS layer for agents, not a replacement host OS or a chatbot wrapper.
design_principles.title: RSI swarm AI OS

design_principles.summary: Mandates 47 and 64; native verified installation and provisioning, with no shell or WSL prerequisite on Windows. Legacy scripts are migration work, not the mandated primary surface.
design_principles.title: One-line install

design_principles.summary: Mandates 48, 53 and 67; agents qualify isolated candidates locally and promote atomically with health checks and rollback. Production is never a development test instance.
design_principles.title: Release-only self-build

foundation_pillars.summary: `TruthTransformer` / `SusiTruthAgent`; models never certify facts. Citation answers resolve through the live ledger; uncited narrative fails when citable receipts exist; an answer with nothing to cite passes only with a visible 'No citations found' warning (unverified by design, commits e8ed3223/6f5bc4d4).
foundation_pillars.title: Truth

foundation_pillars.summary: multi-agent consensus (`susi-gawd`) agent-of-agents orchestrator. Cluster membership identity (`cluster.key`, `node_id`) is installed atomically and self-recovers from an interrupted first start. Operator bans fail closed: a damaged ban list refuses membership instead of reading as empty.
foundation_pillars.title: Swarm

foundation_pillars.summary: Mandate 26 (not naked secrets); traces + blackboard + governance + crown reports + `.susi/receipt_archive.jsonl` (audit-only; truth uses live ledger); secrets redacted (Mandate 38). Task listings never show a phantom Running task: a handle released without an outcome finishes as [ABANDONED], and finished records are pruned oldest-first past 512 while live tasks are kept.
foundation_pillars.title: Glass box

foundation_pillars.summary: append-only HMAC-SHA256 chain (`audit_chain::verify_chain`): cross-process append lock, one-write JSONL records, length-bound atomic tip checkpoints, and fail-closed verification for unreadable/non-UTF-8 input.
foundation_pillars.title: Audit

foundation_pillars.summary: Mandate 44; packs/MCP/models/peers auto-prime (`susi auto`); host installs/keys still gate cloud. First-run host config is always seeded from the defaults compiled into the binary, never from a file in the current directory.
foundation_pillars.title: Zero-config Auto

foundation_pillars.summary: Mandate 37; Safety/Security before parallel fleet (`.susi/last_governance.json`). The privacy posture fails closed: a damaged or unreadable `privacy_mode` enforces `local_only`, and mode switches are persisted atomically or reported as failed. Scoped grants cover only their exact resource, an explicit `*` glob, or children at a `/` boundary (`/srv/ws` never covers `/srv/ws2`). Under `local_only`, HTTP inference providers refuse to send prompts or embedding text to any endpoint off the host/LAN, whatever the provider is named.
foundation_pillars.title: Governance-first

foundation_pillars.summary: `CapabilityRegistry` + extension packs; end-to-end managed catalogs (`susi models` / `frontier` / `openweight` / `agents` / `frameworks` / `mcp` / `openrouter`). MCP admission refuses a damaged or unreadable `mcp_config.json` instead of replacing every configured server with the one being added.
foundation_pillars.title: Pluggable

foundation_pillars.summary: Wasmtime `WasmHost::execute_untrusted_wasm`; Docker `sandbox_exec` when available. Workspace-confined patch cycles preflight every file and roll back through one `TxManager` snapshot; a failed rollback is reported, never claimed as reverted. Transaction ids are reserved on disk, so a fresh process never overwrites another transaction's snapshot, and snapshots are persisted atomically with failures returned. A transaction commits or aborts only against the workspace it snapshotted.
foundation_pillars.title: Sandbox

foundation_pillars.summary: canonical ports 9090–9094 plus a uniform port_offset (env/config); the relative block never drifts.
foundation_pillars.title: Host contract

foundation_pillars.summary: Wasm under the data dir; receipt staging is observable in audits and training reports, claims drop torn lines and train only at a real sample threshold, unlabelable records are skipped instead of stalling the batch, crash-orphans recover oldest-first, and weights publish as hash-bound active/last-known-good generations. A reflex miss escalates to deep reasoning instead of serving a cached apology, and the reflex cache is workspace-scoped and bounded.
foundation_pillars.title: Reflexes

foundation_pillars.summary: `bootstrap_zero_config_substrate` + Candle/weight ladder. Model downloads are verified against the publisher's SHA-256 when one is published (Hugging Face `X-Linked-ETag`) and recorded as provenance that every cold load re-checks; otherwise they are validated structurally only.
foundation_pillars.title: Provision

foundation_pillars.summary: Tokio / Rayon / Crossbeam / parking_lot (Mandates 5, 28–30; lock-preferring, not wait-free absolute).
foundation_pillars.title: Concurrency-first

notes: **`global susi`** — background daemon bound to the host substrate (`~/.susi` / `SusiDirs::substrate_home`), not to a project folder. Owns ports, models, and lock state.
**`susi` CLI** — jailed to the caller's cwd; intents run against that workspace.

**Control plane** — `susi start` / `susi stop` / `susi restart` are deterministic host commands (never natural-language missions). `start` / `restart` wait until ports 9090–9094 answer and print the endpoints.
Per-port config fields stay documentation-only; accessors return the canonical base + `port_offset` (`SUSI_PORT_OFFSET` env wins). `SUSI_HOME` roots a fully isolated second instance.
Peer scouts must not bind 9092 — only the daemon owns the host-contract UDP port.

components.function: Swarm Master Authority: `susi-gawd-agents` 0.1 (fleet/peers/detectors) + `susi-gawd-swarm` 0.1 (AMA/AMAS/DAG) + `susi-gawd-a2a` 0.1 (`ra2a` wire) + `susi-gawd` 0.5 host/governance facade.
Release orchestration, compliance auditing, and axiomatic pulse ingestion.
Substrate maintenance: Hardware audit, model provisioning, and peak selection.

Drift audit: reports intents that recur often enough to be reflex candidates, the workspace experience-buffer and receipt-staging state, and audit-log bottlenecks (reflex latency violations and logged *_FAILED/*_VIOLATION/*_DETECTED events, by type); it reports observations and prescribes nothing. Closes the RSI loop (EV-2022928-314): the hourly substrate audit records the drift report (`DRIFT_AUDIT`) instead of discarding it, and `evolve_recurring_intent` turns a mission intent that recurred 3+ times without a reflex into a `synthesize_capability_for` attempt (model-written reflex, published only after it compiles and runs in the WASI sandbox; else the probe), at most once per intent per 24h, audit-logged as `EVOLUTION_REFLEX_ATTEMPT` with the honest gap report.

Persistent background host bound to `~/.susi`; owns host-contract ports 9090–9094 and spawns from `~/.susi/bin/susi`. Its binary trust anchor (`binary.hash`) is the SHA-256 of the whole binary (read errors fail, never truncate the digest) and is replaced atomically. All 37 of its modules are reachable from a production path (`composition::wire_daemon_os_planes` holds per-peer HMAC gossip on UDP 9095 with HMAC-sealed `gossip_caps.json` (ingress/sealing fail closed when no MAC key exists — no known-key fallback), egress-gated STUN plus TURN Allocate with RFC 5389 MESSAGE-INTEGRITY, and a command-only cloud **version-probe** refreshed every 20th tick that persists `os_planes.json`; `susi os provision` is the explicit list/apply surface; `runtime_admin`'s 10s cycle runs SLA-checked auto-tune over the live task table); the architecture test asserts zero unreachable modules. Discarded probes and type-only references do not count as wiring. Ninety isolated feature sketches and uncalled stub modules have been removed across seven deletion batches: the fifth (EV-2022928-301) removed 17 unreachable modules that duplicated a live feature elsewhere, the sixth (EV-2022928-308) 12 cell-OS sketches with no runtime behind them (those needs live on policy/task/sandbox/checkpoint planes, not resurrected modules), and the seventh removed 32 uncalled blackboard/server/composition stubs (`admin`, `audit_log`, `budget`, `cas`, `cell_snapshot`, `checkpoint`, `code_signing`, `composition_recommender`, `dashboard`, `docs_generator`, `event_log`, `fork`, `hot_reload`, `identity`, `inspector`, `leaderboard`, `load_balancer`, `logger`, `metrics`, `p2p_router`, `plugins`, `signal`, `suspend`, `task_queue`, `tool_catalog`, `tool_proxy`, `topology`, `tracing`, `ttl`, `webhook_dispatcher`, `what_if`, `workflows`). The Devin merge additionally fail-closed host-token seeding (`ensure_api_auth_token_seeded` → `EaiResult`; no binding or leaf/cell spawn without the persisted token) and deleted the three modules reachable only via synthetic snapshot probes.

First-party typed loopback client for the `susi-native` Wasmtime service. Feature planes compile this crate once and never source-mount or link the Wasmtime implementation. The Wasmtime implementation itself is the vendor crate `susi-vendor-wasmtime` (renamed from the `susi-native` crate once its HTTP shell moved to `susi-leaf-services`; the service keeps the name `susi-native`); it also owns the daemon's metered in-process cell runtime and plugin validation (EV-2022928-298), so wasmtime is linked by exactly one crate.

Shared foundation is consumed through real Cargo edges that point down the AGENTS.md leaf order; normal dependencies are not redundantly repeated in dev/build scopes (`paths → error → config → core/sandbox → services → daemon`), enforced by `workspace_edges_follow_the_leaf_order`. The shared HTTP transport exposes status and centrally caps responses; the std-only loopback client caps responses at 16 MiB. `susi-paths` is one crate: `susi-paths` is one crate: `SusiDirs` asks the paths service and falls back to the same local resolver the service answers with. `susi-error` is one crate: every SUSI crate returns the same `susi_error::EaiError`, whose events post to the error service and fall back to the local metrics file (the service process appends directly). `susi-config` is one crate: the global `SusiConfig` read/write prefers the config service and falls back to the local files, the service process always resolves locally, and `cluster_key` signing stays local. `susi-sandbox-client` is one crate: the sandbox IPC client plus the audit-chain, auto-install, daemon-state and manager helpers the `susi-sandbox` service and every client share; bollard is linked only by the service. `susi-core` is one crate: the ten feature planes that used to compile a private `susi_core` module now declare `susi-core = { workspace = true }` and re-export it, so the microkernel is one compiled copy per process rather than one per crate — `susi_core_is_never_source_mounted_into_a_consumer` (`tests/duplication_tests.rs`) makes a relapse a build failure. `susi-abi` is one crate: every plane and cell binary that used to compile a private ABI copy now declares `susi-abi = { workspace = true }` and re-exports it (the shared TCP cell loop lives in the same crate behind the `cell-server` feature) — `susi_abi_is_never_source_mounted_into_a_consumer` makes a relapse a build failure. `susi-gawd-agents` is one crate: the swarm, A2A and host crates that used to remount its fleet/detector sources now declare `susi-gawd-agents = { workspace = true }` and re-export the modules — `susi_gawd_agents_is_never_source_mounted_into_a_consumer` makes a relapse a build failure. `susi-gawd-swarm` and `susi-gawd-a2a` are Cargo dependencies of the host `susi-gawd` crate (the remaining within-plane mounts of those trees were removed). `susi-gemi` depends on `susi-gemi-models` and re-exports it as `models` rather than remounting the catalog sources. `susi-http-transport` is one crate: the TLS-sniffing accept loop, Hyper connection builder, and outbound `http_call` / `http_call_with_body` over crate-private `ureq` that GEMI REST, GMCP, A2A, MCP/peer, and live-search callers share (callers never name `ureq::Agent`); vendor SDKs and provider wire shapes stay in `susi-vendor-*` / `susi-adapters-*`. Core/OS crates (paths/error/config/gawd host/swarm/agents/a2a) must not declare `reqwest`/`ureq`. `susi-vendor-candle` is one crate: Candle, CUDA/Metal/MKL features, the runtime device probe, the Qwen2 GGUF split (forked from candle-transformers), and Hugging Face `tokenizers` live at rank 2 so `susi-gemi` and `susi-gemi-models` share one vendor feature graph, one tokenizer crate, and one process-wide device cache — `susi_vendor_candle_is_never_source_mounted_into_a_consumer` makes a remount a build failure. `susi-adapters-llm` is one crate: SUSI-authored OpenAI / Anthropic / Gemini / Triton wire shapes (not vendored SDKs) live at rank 2; `susi-core` re-exports `inference_wire` — `susi_adapters_llm_is_never_source_mounted_into_a_consumer` makes a remount a build failure. Feature-plane Cargo.toml files no longer re-list cluster-key crypto (ed25519/x25519/chacha20) or other deps that only the deleted source mounts compiled against. The cross-crate `#[path]` mount ratchet is at zero: 159 mounts on 2026-09-28, 0 now. Leaf services (paths, error, config, sandbox, native) are served by `susi-leaf-services`, the only crate where they meet axum: `susi-paths`/`susi-error`/`susi-config` carry no HTTP framework or tokio, `susi-sandbox` keeps only bollard and `susi-native` only wasmtime, one pair of bearer policies (`bearer_authorized` fail-closed, `supervisor_bearer_authorized` env-token) replaces four copies, and every leaf binary resolves its port through `LEAF_SERVICES` (which honours the config-file port offset). Dependency hygiene (EV-2022928-297): no crate declares a dependency it does not use; `susi-paths` depends only on `serde_json` (per-OS user dirs are std-only, reproducing the `directories` layout exactly); `once_cell` and `md5` are gone (std `LazyLock`; the swarm's retry-loop detector compares error text directly); `crossbeam` is gone — the pulse queue uses `flume`, the workspace's one channel crate. Leaf-service clients (EV-2022928-302) share one std-only `susi_paths::loopback` client; `service_port(env, default)` applies the instance offset for every client (config, sandbox and native clients previously used the bare default port, so a dev instance reached the release instance's services). One error model (EV-2022928-310): no library crate declares `anyhow`; susi-agents, susi-gemi, susi-gemi-models and susi-tools return `EaiResult` via `susi_error::{ResultExt, eai_err!, eai_bail!}`; Candle errors convert at the GEMI edge (`engines::candle_err::from_candle`).
Parses the built-in core module manifest list and prints configured port info at startup.
Autonomous environment preparation (Weights & Tools).
Reports the detected hardware profile (CPU, RAM, GPU/acceleration).
Governance auditor and destructive command interceptor.
Credential masking and exfiltration prevention.
Observational drift detector: reports recurrent capability gaps and substrate signals; it does not claim repairs or write code. Verified reflex synthesis is a separate capability-gap path.
MCP JSON-RPC 2.0 endpoint verification.
Live crates.io REST API package scouting.
High-density context manager and workspace analyzer.
Autonomous synthesis and recruitment of specialist agents.
Microsecond intent classification and deterministic neural reflex engine.

Closes capability gaps with hot-loaded WASI reflexes, without a daemon restart (`synthesize_capability`, EV-2022928-313): the local model writes a std-only program for the intent (input = argv[1], result on stdout); it is published as `reflex_<name>` only if it parses (`susi-vendor-syn`), compiles to `wasm32-wasip1`, and runs successfully on a probe input under the `susi-native` WASI sandbox before the rename into the live name. Its correctness for the intent is not verified, and the reply says so. When any step fails it falls back to the signature-echo probe reflex, which proves the hot-load path but does not implement the capability — the reply then says the gap remains open and why functional synthesis failed (`gap_report`).

Hardware-aware local inference host (`susi-gemi::engines::runtime_substrate::InferenceHost`): loads and caches GGUF weights (llama/qwen2 families, GPU layer split when the backend allows); other model formats and hosts are reached through HTTP providers, not loaded natively.

Local/cloud reasoning and placement bridge: crates `susi-gemi-models` (select/provision/lifecycle) + `susi-gemi` engines (run); one policy routes ready local models, configured cloud providers, or explicit models and emits an auditable placement decision id.
Local neural weights (`susi-alpha.safetensors`) for deterministic reflex.
`susi models` (`susi_gemi_models::coding_models`): ranked coding/agent cloud models — list/doctor/setup/configure/prefer/probe.

`susi frontier` (`susi_gemi_models::frontier`): top 5 frontier reasoning engines (Claude 3.5/4 Sonnet, GPT-4o/5, DeepSeek-R1/V3, Gemini 1.5/2.0 Pro, Llama 3/3.1) with variants — list/doctor/setup/prefer/probe.

`susi openweight` (`susi_gemi_models::open_weight`): top open-weight FOSS-adjacent models (DeepSeek-R1/V3, Llama 3.x, Qwen 2.5-Coder, Mistral Nemo/Large, Phi-4) via Ollama/vLLM — list/doctor/pull/prefer/probe.
`susi openrouter` (`susi_gemi_models::openrouter`): OpenRouter credentials, curated routes, prefer pin, and live `/models` probe.

`susi mcp` (`susi_tools::leading_mcp`): durable enable/disable into `~/.susi/mcp_config.json`; editorial top ranks Filesystem, GitHub (official `ghcr.io/github/github-mcp-server`), Context7, Playwright, Sentry (`@sentry/mcp-server`) + Chrome DevTools companion.

`susi agents` / `susi frameworks` (`susi_agents::external`): end-to-end doctor/setup/run/tasks for leading external coding agents and Python engines (OpenHands, Aider, SWE-agent, CrewAI, LangGraph, AutoGen, smolagents, LlamaIndex, Temporal, E2B, Haystack, …).
Host-contract Streamable HTTP on **9090** (`/mcp`, alias `/messages`) and alias **9093**; UDP discovery on **9092**.
CLI proxy acting as a protocol bridge.
Host-contract REST on port **9091** (`susi_paths::ports::GEMI`). External clients may hard-code it; the daemon never randomizes or silently drifts this port (same contract as 9090/9092/9093/9094).
Mission-scoped ledger (`susi-core::capture`): live tool/MCP calls mint `ToolReceipt`s; answers must cite receipt IDs.
Absolute-truth gate (`susi-core::truth`): accepts only ledger citations, compiled reads, or native verified receipts — models never certify facts.
Structured provenance types (`EvidenceRecord`, `Claim`, `EvidenceSource::ToolReceipt`) verified against the live ledger.

Append-only provenance graph (`susi-core::context_graph`) of workspaces, missions, tool calls, patch cycles, and observations; bounded at 32k resident nodes (ephemeral evicted first, in batches down to a 30k low-water mark), compacted by atomic rename, and folded incrementally across processes with the replay cursor bound to the log file's identity. Observation text, labels, and payload strings are credential-redacted on record.

Every third-party SDK is owned by its own `susi-vendor-*` crate; most expose SUSI-shaped APIs without vendor types, while the MCP server facade currently re-exports rmcp protocol/macro types required by GMCP: `susi-vendor-candle` (Candle, tokenizers, CUDA/Metal/MKL, device probe), `susi-vendor-wasmtime` (Wasmtime/WASI reflexes + metered, memory-capped in-process cells + plugin validation), `susi-vendor-mcp` (rmcp MCP client + reqwest streamable-HTTP transport, pooled, lease-bounded), `susi-vendor-tantivy` (full-text `DocIndex`), `susi-vendor-fastembed` (one process-wide embedding model shared by the capability provider and semantic index; provider health reflects cached model-load failure), `susi-vendor-chrome` (headless Chrome page capture). Policy stays with SUSI callers (URL/SSRF checks, lease budgets from `SusiConfig`, index watermarks). `core_os_crates_must_not_declare_http_clients` is an allow-list: only `susi-http-transport` and `susi-vendor-*`/`susi-adapters-*` may declare reqwest/ureq. `susi-vendor-syn` (EV-2022928-300) owns runtime Rust parsing (the bloat auditor in susi-gawd and gmcp's `ast_analyze` no longer each link syn); its metrics exclude nested test-only `cfg(all(test, ...))` code without exempting `cfg(any(test, ...))` production branches; `ra2a` stays confined to `susi-gawd-a2a`, whose whole job is the A2A adapter.

mandates.imperative: Never lie about what happened. Self-reported status, execution outcomes, test results, and known limitations must always match reality, even when the truth is a failure. Example (2026-09-27): the autonomous planner reported '(transaction rolled back)' after aborting a transaction that had snapshotted no files; the claim was removed rather than kept as reassurance.
mandates.title: No Lies

mandates.imperative: Never fabricate a fact, API, file, or code reference that wasn't verified by reading it. An unverified claim must be stated as unverified, not asserted.
mandates.title: No Hallucinations

mandates.imperative: Continuously audit for and eliminate technical bloat (dead code, oversized functions, unjustified `.unwrap()`/`.clone()` density, config/behavior drift). `BloatAuditor` (`susi bloat-audit`) is the enforcement mechanism, not a formality. A bare "100% bloat-free forever" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — this mandate is continuous rejection via measurable audit, not an unverifiable absolute clean state.
mandates.title: Bloat Rejection (Continuous Audit)

mandates.imperative: A *client* (CLI caller, IDE, HTTP/MCP caller) must never be left waiting past 2ms for acknowledgment — this governs the client-facing response, not the total wall-clock time of the work itself; see Mandate 32 for how that's achieved (instant return, streaming, or an async task handle). Internal primitive operations (a lock acquisition, a config read, a hashmap lookup) should stay sub-millisecond, but a multi-agent swarm mission's true completion time is bounded by inference and I/O, not this mandate — measuring end-to-end mission latency against a 2ms ceiling produces guaranteed, meaningless "violation" telemetry on every non-trivial mission and must not be done (see Mandate 26).
mandates.title: Sub-2ms Client Reflex (Ack, Not Mission Done)

mandates.imperative: On the swarm execution path, prefer non-blocking concurrency: atomics, lock-free structures (`DashMap`), channels (Crossbeam/CSP), and `parking_lot` only when a mutex is required. Blocking `std::sync` locks and long holds on the Rayon/Tokio critical path are discouraged. Exceptions are allowed when labeled and bounded (e.g. `tokio::task::spawn_blocking` for sync I/O, short critical sections). A bare "blocking locks prohibited everywhere / zero blocking ever" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — this mandate is lock-*preferring* swarm design, not a proof of a fully wait-free process.
mandates.title: Lock-Preferring Swarm Path (Not Zero Blocking)

mandates.imperative: Maintain a highly critical evaluation mode for code, architecture, and logic.
mandates.title: Brutally Honest & Critical

mandates.imperative: A fact verified once (a file's contents, a config value, a running process's state) can go stale mid-task. Re-check assumptions against current codebase and runtime state before acting on them, especially after any action that could have changed that state.
mandates.title: Continuous Re-Verification

mandates.imperative: Source code and empirical runtime results outrank prior training knowledge, memory, or assumption. When they conflict, the freshly-read source or the freshly-run result wins, and prior belief is discarded, not defended. Mission completion requires absolute evidence only: live `EvidenceSession` / `ToolReceipt` citations, compiled binary reads, or native verified receipts — models never certify facts (`TruthTransformer`).
mandates.title: Epistemic Chain of Truth

mandates.imperative: Keep code, documentation, and comments professional and technical — prefer precise, dense prose over marketing filler. A bare "zero filler forever" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 (filler is subjective and not mechanically measurable); this mandate is a style target enforced by review and Mandate 6, not a count of zero adjectives.
mandates.title: Professional Technical Standard

mandates.imperative: Do not leak tokens, credentials, API keys, or sensitive configuration in logs, telemetry, mission traces, or outbound tool content. Durable records must pass Mandate 38 (`SecurityDetector::redact`) before write. A bare "zero tolerance / never leak any secret shape" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — detection is pattern- and config-based, not omniscient; unknown secret formats may require config updates. Intentional non-leak plus redaction is the mandate, not perfect cryptography of every possible secret. The error-metrics sink masks environment credentials and the bundled secret-token patterns before recording any error text. The security veto also rejects any action carrying the value of a credential this process holds (`*_API_KEY`/`*_TOKEN`/`*_SECRET`), whatever its prefix. Secret patterns match only where a token starts (not inside words such as `risk-` or `task-`), in both the veto and the redactor.
mandates.title: No Secret Leaks (Pattern Redaction, Not Omniscience)

mandates.imperative: Shipped production paths must be functional — no hard-coded mockups or placeholders that present as real success. Tests, fixtures, stubs, and harness doubles are allowed when labeled as such (`#[cfg(test)]`, clear stub names). A bare "no placeholders anywhere in the repo" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1; this mandate forbids silent fake-success in operator-facing and daemon paths (aligned with Mandate 44 diagnosable gates).
mandates.title: Real Working Code (Not Silent Fakes)

mandates.imperative: Physical hardware capacity bounds compute and memory: saturate CPU/GPU topologies responsibly and prevent OOM proactively. Hardware is **not** the sole limit — rate limits, bearer auth (Mandate 40), governance (Mandate 37), evidence gates, and operator prefer pins also constrain work. A bare "hardware is the only ceiling" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Hardware Authority (Bounded by Governance Too)

mandates.imperative: Sustain a continuous, resilient background process bound to the host substrate, owning the hard-contract ports 9090–9094 (GMCP/GEMI/UDP/alias/A2A) plus models and lock state. Never silently remap those ports.
mandates.title: Daemon Persistence

mandates.imperative: Autonomously provision the highest-ranking open-source neural weights compatible with detected hardware **when policy allows** (`bootstrap_zero_config_substrate` / model ladder), honoring prefer pins, no-download / offline flags, and disk limits. A bare "always download the absolute highest weights" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — priming is best-effort under Mandate 44 gates, not forced saturation of every host.
mandates.title: Substrate Priming (Policy-Gated)

mandates.imperative: Validate the dynamic agent registry via timestamp-based audits to prevent stale behavior injection.
mandates.title: Registry Hot-Reload

mandates.imperative: Adapt runtime structure and agent composition from empirical swarm outcomes (registry hot-reload, reflex synthesis, mission feedback) — not from unconstrained invention. Adaptation remains bounded by Mandates 37 (governance-first), 41 (untrusted input), 25/36 (destructive guards), and 46 (autonomy under evidence). A bare "Absolute Sovereignty / unconstrained synthesis" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Empirical Adaptation (Governance-Bounded)

mandates.imperative: Prefer spawning parallel sub-swarms for separable atomic components and joining on convergence when that improves throughput or clarity. Sequential or single-agent dispatch remains correct for small goals, governance-only checks, or when parallelism would add noise. A bare "always parallel sub-swarms" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Recursive Decomposition (When Beneficial)

mandates.imperative: Persist mission-relevant state (blackboard, traces, receipts, neural/mission checkpoints where implemented) so interrupted work can resume or be diagnosed. A bare "universal crash-proof recovery of every swarm" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — persistence coverage is best-effort and path-dependent; missing checkpoints must fail honestly, not invent resumed success.
mandates.title: Mission Persistence (Best-Effort Checkpoints)

mandates.imperative: Prefer asynchronous messaging (Pub-Sub, Actor/CSP channels, Crossbeam queues) for multi-agent orchestration. Short synchronous local calls remain allowed on hot paths where a channel would be pure overhead. A bare "all messaging must be async" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Decoupled Messaging (Prefer Async)

mandates.imperative: Self-modification workflow strictly follows: Motion (the triggering intent) -> Architecture (design) -> Structure (implementation) -> Logic (verification). Not to be confused with the release "Motion Rule" (Pillar IV item 3), a distinct local release sequence that happens to share the word "Motion" — the two were previously both called "The Motion Rule," a naming collision that made this document self-contradictory about what "The Motion Rule" means.
mandates.title: Alpha-Self Evolution Order

mandates.imperative: Resolve operator intents via dynamic registries, config, and control-plane routing (`CapabilityRegistry`, extension packs, agent/framework/MCP/model planes) rather than hard-coded goal enums. A bare "Continuous Intent Manifold" slogan without a defined substrate mechanism is forbidden by Mandate 1 — this mandate names the real resolution surface, not an undefined manifold.
mandates.title: Dynamic Intent Resolution

mandates.imperative: Autonomously recover from structural pathologies, memory faults, or a *stale susi* process holding a host-contract port (Sovereign Eviction / reclaim). Host-contract ports themselves never randomize or drift to ephemeral alternatives — if a foreign process owns 9090–9094, bind fails closed.
mandates.title: Self-Healing Reflex

mandates.imperative: Protocol-agnostic admission via registries and config — OpenAI-compat / Anthropic / Gemini / Triton engines, MCP (stdio/HTTP), and peer agents (`managed` / `cli` / `openai_chat` / `http` / `a2a`). No static domain logic in core; local Candle remains llama/qwen2 GGUF-scoped.
mandates.title: Substrate Purity

mandates.imperative: SUSI is licensed under Apache 2.0, in perpetuity, per the terms in `LICENSE` (this is a statement of licensing fact, not a behavioral instruction to follow).
mandates.title: Eternal Liberty

mandates.imperative: Every code path capable of a destructive filesystem, git, or process operation — not only tool-call arguments passed through `exec_command` — must be checked against `SafetyDetector`'s destructive-command patterns (e.g. `rm -rf /`, `rm -rf ~`) before it runs, and any such operation must additionally require an explicit, unambiguous intent sentinel rather than firing on incidental keyword presence in free-text goal input (see Mandate 41). A destructive-pattern list that isn't wired to every place capable of performing that class of operation is a guard that only looks like one; this was found violated in practice (`AdminAgent`'s uninstall action performed an `rm -rf`-equivalent on `~/.susi` without ever consulting `SafetyDetector`, reachable by any goal string containing the word "remove") and fixed, but the general principle — audit coverage must match capability, not just intent — is the actual mandate.
mandates.title: Destructive Command Guard

mandates.imperative: Reasoning steps, tool calls, and state mutations that SUSI performs must be **inspectable through telemetry** — mission protocol output, `.susi/last_mission_trace.json`, `.susi/last_blackboard.json`, governance reports, crown reports, and receipt provenance (`.susi/receipt_archive.jsonl` is audit-only; truth authority remains the live evidence ledger). Telemetry must reflect **real** calls and outcomes (no aspirational narration of work that did not run). Visibility is **bounded**: Mandate 10 / Mandate 38 require secret-token patterns redacted before durable write — redact the secret, do not suppress the surrounding record. This mandate does **not** require exposing provider/model internals (raw logits, vendor system prompts) or unredacted credential bodies. A bare "100% transparency" claim (including naked secrets or third-party internals) is forbidden by Mandate 1 — this mandate is glass-box *inspectability of SUSI's own steps*, not omniscient disclosure.
mandates.title: Glass Box Transparency (Not Naked Secrets)

mandates.imperative: Every operator-visible or audited action must be uniquely identifiable and attributable in telemetry/audit — to a specific agent, tool call, receipt, or genomic reflex when one produced it. A bare "every action is a genomic reflex" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1; reflexes are one attribution class among agents/tools/receipts (see Mandates 26 and 38).
mandates.title: Action Accountability (Agent/Tool/Receipt)

mandates.imperative: Default to `tokio` for non-blocking I/O and daemon/HTTP concurrency. Sync or `spawn_blocking` paths are allowed when the API is inherently blocking and the block is isolated. A bare "tokio for all operations forever" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Async Defaults (Tokio Prefer)

mandates.imperative: Utilize `rayon` for CPU-bound parallel loops and recursive fork-join partitioning on the swarm/fleet path. Sequential loops remain correct for tiny workloads or when Rayon would oversubscribe. A bare "rayon for every loop" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Data Parallelism (Rayon Prefer)

mandates.imperative: When a mutex is required (atomics insufficient), prefer `parking_lot` over `std::sync` Mutex/RwLock in first-party runtime. `std::sync` and other locks remain acceptable at FFI/OS boundaries or when an external crate forces them. A bare "parking_lot exclusively everywhere" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Locking Standard (parking_lot Prefer)

mandates.imperative:
The substrate exists in exactly two operational forms:
- **`global susi` (The Background Service)**: The persistent background daemon (`susi.service` / `daemon-start`) bound to `SusiDirs::substrate_home` (`~/.susi`). Manages CPU/GPU saturation, OS environment care, hard-contract network ports (9090 GMCP `/mcp`, 9091 GEMI, 9092 A2A UDP, 9093 GMCP alias, 9094 A2A HTTP), and central model weights (`~/.susi/models`). World-facing HTTP is not jailed to cwd (see Mandate 40 and the Host contract section).
- **`susi` (Workspace-Scoped CLI)**: The single canonical binary invocation (`~/.susi/bin/susi`) treats the active working directory (`cwd`) as the mission/workspace context for tasks, `susi admin` when operating on that tree, and `susi repo` when `cwd` is the engine source — workspace changes go through transactional patch cycles (`susi tx`, `apply_patch_cycle`) while the daemon owns ports, models, and lock state.
"Jailed to cwd" means **workspace scoping for missions and local artifacts**, not an OS chroot/seccomp cage of the whole process. A bare "unconditionally OS-jailed" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1.
mandates.title: Strict 2-Form Substrate Axiom (Not OS Chroot)

mandates.imperative: Client-facing interactions (IDE, CLI ack, MCP, HTTP/REST, external agents) must not block the caller on full mission completion: return an instant acknowledgment (Mandate 4 Sub-2ms client reflex), stream live telemetry, or yield a background task handle immediately. Hard execution leases and cancellation must terminate unresponsive work before client timeouts. Wall-clock swarm/inference time is **not** required to be <2ms — measuring end-to-end mission latency against that ceiling produces meaningless "violations" (see Mandate 4). A bare "NEVER wait / instant by design for all work" claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — this mandate is non-blocking *client surfaces*, not zero-latency compute. Idle leases are learned per task category from the measured gap between progress reports (5x the worst observed gap, floored by `execution_lease_secs`); a category with fewer than three completed samples is not leased. Calibration is persisted atomically; a lost or unparseable history is recorded as an error, not silently reset. Progress is what a task observably produces (e.g. bytes from an agent command's pipes), never a timer ticking on its behalf.
mandates.title: Client Non-Blocking Surfaces (Not Instant Work)

mandates.imperative: When Susi develops Susi, synchronize version manifests and build an identified candidate in private state. Deploy to the canonical production path only after the native local qualification and atomic promotion gates in Mandates 48, 53 and 67 pass. A source edit, version bump or new binary signature never authorizes a hot-swap by itself. Preserve the running builder and previous verified artifact; report toolchain or network failures accurately.
mandates.title: Synchronized Substrate Versioning (Repo/Release Paths)

mandates.imperative:
- **`susi swarm`**: Agent-of-agents orchestration via lock-preferring CSP channels and Rayon work-stealing parallel agent dispatch across available host CPU cores (GPU used when inference backends allow — not a claim of saturating every GPU on every mission).
- **`susi engine`**: Races Candle (llama/qwen2 GGUF) against OpenAI-compatible local/cloud engines (and Anthropic/Gemini/Triton via config) through `CapabilityRegistry` — not a claim of native SafeTensors/ONNX chat weights.
- **`susi models` (+ frontier / openweight / openrouter)**: Non-blocking resumable background downloads and dynamic Hugging Face discovery for the progressive model ladder, **and** durable end-to-end control planes for curated catalogs — coding/agent cloud models (`susi models`), top 5 frontier reasoning engines (`susi frontier`: Claude Sonnet, GPT-4o/5, DeepSeek-R1/V3, Gemini Pro, Llama 3/3.1), open-weight FOSS-adjacent hosts (`susi openweight` via Ollama/vLLM), and OpenRouter routes (`susi openrouter`). Parallel durable planes manage leading external agents/frameworks (`susi agents` / `susi frameworks`) and MCP servers (`susi mcp`; top ranks Filesystem, GitHub, Context7, Playwright, Sentry + Chrome DevTools). Catalogs load via extension packs (`Mandate 35`); no subscriptions are provisioned implicitly.
A bare "maximum hardware power / excellence" marketing claim is forbidden by Mandate 1 — these pillars name real control planes and engines, not unbounded saturation.
mandates.title: Three Innovation Pillars (Swarm / Engine / Models)

mandates.imperative: All models, providers, agents, tools, and MCP servers must be integrated via dynamic Traits, lock-free Registries (`DashMap`), and runtime JSON/TOML configuration (`config.json`). Hardcoding static vendor strings or model enums in Rust source as the *only* admission path is prohibited. Adding a new model, tool, or provider must be doable via configuration or self-registering traits without editing core admission enums. Concretely: `SusiConfig` (`crates/susi-sandbox/src/manager.rs`) is the reference implementation — its root is a `#[serde(flatten)] DynamicRegistry` (`HashMap<String, Value>`), not a closed struct with named fields, and even its nested typed sub-structs (e.g. `ModelLadderConfigStep`) pair named convenience fields with their own flatten catch-all so an unrecognized key is never silently dropped. Every config-shaped struct — anything read from and, especially, written back to a user-editable JSON file — must follow the same pattern. This is not a theoretical concern: `McpServerConfig`/`McpConfig` (`crates/susi-tools/src/config.rs`) had no flatten catch-all until found and fixed (`EV-2022920-046`) — `auto_configure_server`'s read-modify-write cycle on `mcp_config.json` would have silently deleted any field a user hand-added ahead of susi's own support for it. This does not extend to fixed-shape protocol or internal telemetry structs (JSON-RPC envelopes, hardware/evidence reports) that are not user-editable config surfaces — those are correctly typed and closed. **Exception (Host contract):** public ports 9090–9094 are intentional compile-time constants in `susi_paths::ports` and are not user-overridable — Mandate 35 forbids inventing *vendor/model* hardcodes, not freezing the external client port contract. A bare "100% dynamic config / zero hardcoded structs" slogan is forbidden by Mandate 1 while typed protocol structs and host-contract constants remain necessary. Example (2026-09-27): natural-intent classification now reads `intent_classify` from config; its hard-coded copy of those lists was removed.
mandates.title: Dynamic Config Registries (Not Zero Typed Structs)

mandates.imperative: `SafetyDetector` (`crates/susi-gawd-agents/src/safety.rs`) audits an action's command text against configured destructive-command patterns and critical-system-path patterns before it is allowed to run. This backs Mandate 25 and is what `SafetyAgent` (Pillar II) enforces.
mandates.title: Pre-Execution Destructive Pattern Guard

mandates.imperative: In any swarm dispatch, `SafetyAgent` and `SecurityAgent` must clear the goal before any execution-capable agent in the same mission is allowed to run — they never race in the same parallel batch as execution-capable agents, since a destructive or leaking action could otherwise complete before the veto lands. This is a scheduling guarantee, not just a policy statement: governance agents are dispatched and awaited first.
mandates.title: Governance-First Sequencing

mandates.imperative: Text that will be persisted to telemetry, audit logs, or any other durable record must have configured secret-token patterns redacted (`SecurityDetector::redact`) before it is written — not merely blocked at the point of an explicit "send this secret" action. Mandate 26 (glass-box inspectability of SUSI steps) and Mandate 10 (no secret leaks) both hold: redact the secret, don't suppress the surrounding record.
mandates.title: Credential Masking

mandates.imperative: `SecurityDetector` audits outbound-shaped action text against configured exfiltration-vector patterns (e.g. suspicious URLs, known exfiltration endpoints) before the action runs, independent of and in addition to the secret-pattern check in Mandate 38.
mandates.title: Exfiltration Prevention

mandates.imperative: Any network-facing HTTP surface (GMCP HTTP, GEMI REST, or any future equivalent) must support a required bearer-token check (`api_auth_token`) and a per-client rate limit (`rate_limit_per_minute`), both config-driven and both checked before any route is dispatched except CORS preflight and an unauthenticated liveness probe. The daemon **seeds** a host token on first start (`SusiConfig::ensure_api_auth_token_seeded` → `~/.susi/api_token`, mode 0600, `O_EXCL` install so a concurrent seeder's token wins); when a token is configured, every HTTP peer (including localhost) must present `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Seeding fails closed: a symlink or non-regular token path, an empty or unreadable token file, a failed CSPRNG, or any I/O error returns `Err`, and the daemon refuses to bind host-contract ports or spawn leaf services/cells without the persisted token — no weak in-memory fallback ever authenticates peers. Before seeding, non-loopback peers are denied (fail closed on the wire). A world-facing surface with no way to require authentication is not a theoretical gap — this substrate shipped with exactly that gap until it was found and closed. The per-client limit buckets IPv6 by /64 and IPv4-mapped IPv6 as IPv4, so address rotation within one allocation cannot bypass it.
mandates.title: World-Facing Surface Authentication

mandates.imperative: Goal/intent text and any LLM-synthesized artifact derived from it (a specialist agent's `description`, a tool argument, a blackboard entry) must be treated as adversarial once it can originate from an unauthenticated or external caller. Concretely: (a) a mutating or destructive operation must never fire on incidental keyword presence in free-text goal input — it requires an explicit, unambiguous intent sentinel (the `admin pulse:` prefix convention); (b) any agent profile synthesized by an LLM from goal text must be sanitized (bounded field lengths, `is_core` forced false, governance-checked) before it is persisted or ever fed back into a future mission's prompt, since persisted state becomes part of every subsequent mission that recruits it. This mandate exists because both failure modes were found present in shipped code and fixed; it generalizes the fix so the same class of bug can't recur in a new code path.
mandates.title: Untrusted Input Boundary

mandates.imperative: Zero `.unwrap()`/`.expect()`/`panic!()` in non-test code, except at a call site carrying a comment stating the specific invariant that makes the panic path unreachable (e.g. "safe: length checked above", "safe: regex is a compile-time literal"). Everywhere else, the fallible path must propagate a real `Result`/`EaiResult` via `?` rather than crash the calling thread — this substrate's daemon and swarm-dispatch paths (Mandate 5, Mandate 13) cannot afford an unrecoverable panic from what should have been a recoverable error. `#[cfg(test)]` code is explicitly exempt: an `.unwrap()` on a known-good test fixture is idiomatic and correct, not a violation — this mandate governs production code paths, not test assertions. This is phrased as a scoped rule rather than a bare "no unwrap, ever" specifically because the latter would be false today (269 call sites existed in `src/` when this mandate was written) and Mandate 1 (No Lies) forbids writing a false claim into this document; this mandate is the target an ongoing triage is converging on, not a claim of present compliance. Four triage batches so far: `EV-2022920-047` (`net_guard.rs` found already fully compliant despite a raw count of 7 — every site inside `#[cfg(test)]`; `reflex_synth.rs` had 3 real non-test sites, 2 fixed and 1 given a justifying comment), `EV-2022920-048` (`qwen2_split.rs` also found already fully compliant despite a raw count of 51; `daemon/server.rs`'s 2 real non-test sites fixed — notably `run_daemon_loop`'s config-load `.expect()`, more severe than a typical unwrap because `panic = "abort"` means it aborted the whole daemon process, not just a thread), `EV-2022920-049` (`agents.rs`'s and `speculative.rs`'s one and two real non-test sites respectively, both verified genuinely safe by construction and comment-justified rather than rewritten), and `EV-2022920-050` (`bloat_audit.rs` found to have zero real sites — its raw count of 42 was almost entirely the tool's own report-label strings describing unwrap/expect/clone counts, not actual calls; `manager.rs`'s 4 real sites are all the same bundled-default-JSON pattern, comment-justified once and referenced from the other three rather than repeated). A fifth batch (EV-2022922-098) checked `.expect(`/`panic!(` across eight more crates (susi-sandbox, susi-gemi, susi-gemi-models, susi-agents, susi-core, susi-gawd, susi-gmcp, susi-gawd-agents) plus re-checked `.unwrap()` in susi-core/susi-agents specifically, and found only 14 real non-test sites total across all of that (not the dozens the earlier "~139 remain" estimate implied for a batch of this size) — 6 already carried a Mandate 42 justification comment (sandbox/manager.rs x5, susi-agents/registry.rs x1), and the remaining 8 (susi-sandbox/extensions.rs x5, susi-core/bus.rs x2, susi-core/truth.rs x1) were verified genuinely safe by construction and given one. Zero open non-test sites remain in those eight crates as of this batch. The old "~139 remain" figure predates this batch, was never re-derived from a full re-grep, and should not be trusted as current — five crates (susi-daemon, susi-gawd-swarm, susi-server, susi-tools, susi-native) have not yet been split into real vs. test-only sites at all, so the true remaining count is presently unknown rather than ~139; the next batch should start there.
mandates.title: Fallible Error Handling

mandates.imperative: SUSI and its distributed ecosystem must be implemented in Rust, including runtime, build orchestration, installers, integration and release tooling; Rust-produced Wasm is permitted. Required C/C++ or other-language implementation dependencies must be replaced, not hidden behind Rust facades or renamed as optional peers. Host operating-system ABI calls and use of the installed Rust compiler/linker are platform boundaries, not permission to bundle a non-Rust runtime. Remote protocol services are outside the Susi executable and must be identified accurately; optional foreign programs must never be required for the compliant Susi path. Existing non-Rust source or dependencies are migration defects, not exemptions. Mandates 63 and 68 define verification and license coverage. A requirement is not evidence of current compliance (Mandate 1).
mandates.title: Rust-Only Susi Implementation

mandates.imperative: Normal installation, first run, model/provider discovery, local/cloud routing, agent scheduling, build isolation and upgrades must work without user-written configuration or manual technical setup. Detect host capabilities and select safe defaults; preserve explicit user preferences and fail visibly when a capability is unavailable. Agents repair setup defects rather than handing technical steps to the CEO. Credentials, paid-service authorization, spending limits, privacy preferences and destructive-action authorization remain explicit boundaries; never invent, scrape or purchase credentials. Optional advanced controls do not excuse required configuration on the default path. Measure clean-machine and offline first-run behavior before declaring this requirement met (Mandate 70).
mandates.title: Zero User-Written Configuration

mandates.imperative: SUSI is the **RSI swarm AI OS** for hosting, provisioning, and managing any local and cloud AI ecosystem — not a chatbot wrapper and not a general-purpose host operating system. Locally it hosts and provisions host-resident models/runtimes, GPU/CPU placement, MCP tools, sandboxed reflexes, workspace memory, and agents. For cloud it admits configured provider, MCP, A2A, and managed CLI peers through the same capability, budget, evidence, audit, privacy, and placement contracts; credentials stay operator-owned. One placement policy chooses ready local, configured cloud, or an explicit model and emits a decision id resolvable to the signed `INFERENCE_PLACEMENT` audit record. Recursive self-improvement is scoped (Mandate 1): receipt-backed reflex distillation runs unattended; code self-patching is gated (`apply_patch_cycle` / Mandate 48 self-build); agents own authorized source changes end-to-end without requiring human implementation or code review; promotion still requires the local verified release gate (Mandates 62, 67 and 71). Concretely the layer means: persistent `global susi` daemon bound to `~/.susi`, fixed host-contract ports 9090–9094, evidence-gated agent-of-agents swarm (GAWD), model/MCP/peer admission and control planes, HMAC audit, Wasmtime/Docker sandbox, reflexes, and crown-verifiable Tier S pillars. Outbound JSON HTTP is owned by `susi-http-transport` (the only workspace crate that declares `ureq`); callers use `http_call` / `http_call_with_body` and never name `ureq::Agent`. Core, adapters-llm, gmcp, agents, and the daemon call that transport rather than vendor HTTP clients. Cloud inference (OpenAI-compat, Anthropic, Gemini, Triton) is hosted through `susi-gemi::HttpProvider` over `susi-http-transport`, not a vendor SDK. The live in-process swarm-host components are wired from `susi-daemon::composition` and surfaced on `susi os`; the daemon loop constructs host OS planes (`wire_daemon_os_planes`) and drives them on a 30s tick (gossip fanout, STUN/TURN, cell reaping, capability policy grants, supervision, and cloud CLI version-probe), persisting `os_planes.json` so the CLI process can read the report. Swarm gossip binds instance UDP 9095 (`ports::GOSSIP`, listed in `ports::SWARM_UDP`, **not** in the 9090–9094 host-contract tuple — 9092 stays A2A discovery), HMAC-seals datagrams with a *per-peer* MAC derived from the cluster-key `susi-gossip-v1` key (`susi-gossip-peer-v1:{node_id}`; process-local fallback — if neither cluster key nor OS entropy exists there is no MAC key and sealing/ingress fail closed rather than use a known key), and persists capabilities in HMAC-sealed `gossip_caps.json`. NAT still accepts `SUSI_PUBLIC_IP`; when unset the daemon runs STUN `discover_default` only while `mac_policy::egress_permitted` allows external egress (or an explicit `SUSI_TURN_*` relay is configured), recording DNS/timeout failures without pretending Open. Symmetric or failed STUN takes a TURN path (`SUSI_TURN_SERVER` Allocate with RFC 5389 MESSAGE-INTEGRITY via `SUSI_TURN_USER`/`SUSI_TURN_PASS`, or `SUSI_TURN_RELAY` for an already-allocated relay). Cloud VM/k8s provision/manage is `susi-vendor-cloud` (kubectl/docker/aws/gcloud/az CLIs — no vendor SDKs in core). The 30s tick only version-probes those CLIs; `susi os provision list|apply` is the explicit live-API surface. The MCP server SDK (`rmcp`) lives in `susi-vendor-mcp-server`; GMCP never declares it. The architecture ratchet counts only actual production references, not discarded probes or type-only mentions. It runs **on** Linux / macOS / native Windows (WSL is not a Windows prerequisite), does not replace the host kernel, init, package manager, or desktop, and must never be documented or marketed as "the computer's OS" or a drop-in replacement for Linux/macOS/Windows. Public wording must prefer "RSI swarm AI OS" / "OS layer for AI agents" / "agent-of-agents substrate" (as in `README.md` and verified product claims) over unbounded "OS for AI" slogans. Absolute replacement-OS language is forbidden by Mandate 1; this mandate is the citable DNA form of that product boundary.
mandates.title: RSI Swarm AI OS (Not a Host OS, Not a Chatbot Wrapper)

mandates.imperative: Given an authorized intent, SUSI agents plan, implement, test, debug, integrate and complete the outcome end-to-end. Do not require the CEO to inspect code, perform technical steps or provide per-step engineering approvals. Use parallel isolated agents for separable work and resolve implementation issues autonomously. Honor scope, user stop instructions, credential and spending permissions, destructive-action authorization and the Safety/Security/Truth/Evidence gates. Missing evidence or a failed check cannot be reported as COMPLETE. Agent-only engineering is a requirement; it is not a claim that every mission succeeds or that user authorization boundaries disappear.
mandates.title: Agent-Owned Autonomous Execution

mandates.imperative: Installation and provisioning must use native Rust tooling with verified artifact hashes, native paths and automatic discovery. Windows must not require Bash, WSL, MSYS, Python, Node or a container to install, build, test or run Susi. Prefer verified prebuilt artifacts and support a local native source build. GitHub hosting is optional distribution, never a prerequisite for debug builds or development. Legacy install.sh/install.ps1/build-gpu.sh paths are compatibility migration work, not exceptions to Rust-only implementation. Preserve the canonical production binary, explicit download/spend authorization and diagnosable failures; native first-run success must be demonstrated on a clean machine.
mandates.title: Native Installation and Provisioning

mandates.imperative: The installed production Susi remains the stable toolchain that builds its successor. Agents build debug and optimized candidates in their own private target directories and test them in separate per-agent scratch homes with isolated state, ports, credentials and daemon lifecycles. Never test against or overwrite the running production instance. A shared ~/.susi-dev default is insufficient for concurrent agents. Promote only a candidate that passed Mandates 53, 67 and 71 through the native local promotion path with atomic replacement, retained previous artifact, health verification and rollback. A debug build, successful compilation, GitHub tag or model assertion is not production authorization. First installation is a separate verified native path. Existing release-sync scripts must be migrated; their existence does not exempt them from Mandates 63–67.
mandates.title: Self-Build Order and Isolated Candidates

mandates.imperative: Every agent works in its own git worktree and branch with unique identity, private build output and isolated runtime state; never edit the primary checkout or share a writable target directory. Reserve disjoint file/directory scopes before editing. The local workflow is atomic per task: observe the local integration head, reserve ownership, implement, verify, commit, integrate under serialization, verify the actual merged tree, then close and release. Use cargo local-workflow (xtask/src/bin/local-workflow.rs) for available local reservations and guarded commits; complete missing harness/integration behavior rather than assuming it exists. GitHub, origin/main freshness, network claims, shell hooks and remote CI are not prerequisites. CLAUDE.md, GEMINI.md and .github/copilot-instructions.md must point to AGENTS.md without duplicating contradictory rules. Preserve dirty worktrees and other agents' changes. Fast-forward the primary only after verified local integration; never force-push, delete main or bypass evidence gates.
mandates.title: Isolated Local Worktree Workflow

mandates.imperative: Record work as one task file per record under .agents/tasks/ with unique T-<AGENT>-<n> identifiers, dependencies, declared scopes and meaningful acceptance. One live claim at a time per worker. Reservations must be atomic across the coordinating repository and reject overlapping paths, including Windows aliases; cross-host work requires one shared coordinator. Each commit must be attributable to its owned task (Task: T-<AGENT>-<n>, or the native local launcher's Task: LOCAL-<name> scope receipt during migration). A commit or scope receipt is not test evidence. A task closes only after its nonempty acceptance and integrated-tree verification pass on the actual local integration head; zero tests do not count. Failure or crash preserves ownership and evidence until deliberate recovery. No remote receipt, network availability, GitHub merge or human code review is required for local completion. Never close a multi-requirement task merely because one tooling test passed.
mandates.title: Locally Verifiable Task Ownership

mandates.imperative: Parallel agents reserve disjoint edits and never share writable worktrees, build outputs, runtime homes or ports. Shared state is append-only or one-file-per-record with namespaced EV-<AGENT>-<n> and T-<AGENT>-<n> identities. On evidence/identity conflicts, union the entries; never delete or renumber another agent's evidence. Validate structured records with native parsers. Scope checks must inspect staged, unstaged and untracked changes, including renames. Integrate one candidate at a time against the current local head and test the resulting combined tree; a clean textual merge is not behavioral proof. Conflict recovery belongs to agents, not the CEO. Cooperative reservations alone do not justify a universally conflict-free claim.
mandates.title: Non-Conflicting Shared State

mandates.imperative: Tests and development agents must not read or mutate production state: ~/.susi, shared ~/.susi-dev, inherited SUSI_HOME/SUSI_PORT_OFFSET, real provider credentials, cooldowns, routing preferences or evidence files. Each test process receives a unique scratch home, Windows USERPROFILE/HOME and XDG paths, isolated ports and scrubbed credentials; process-global environment changes require synchronization and restoration. Read-only toolchain/dependency caches may be shared, writable build/runtime state may not. Verify that tests leave production untouched and do not rely on network services unless explicitly classified and provisioned. Native local checks must enforce this; scripts/check-hermetic-tests.sh is legacy coverage, not a required Windows shell dependency.
mandates.title: Hermetic Tests and Per-Agent Runtime Isolation

mandates.imperative: Production candidates must pass a native local gate on a clean, identified source tree: locked dependency and license audit, Rust-only graph/source checks, formatting, clippy, required nonempty tests, freshly built executable smoke tests (including E2E_CHECKS where applicable), artifact digest and provenance, then health-checked atomic promotion with rollback to the previous verified artifact. Bind evidence to the source tree, dependency lock, toolchain, target and feature set; never reuse stale proof after changes. Agents perform this work under the authorized product mandate; no human code review or GitHub run is a completion prerequisite. Local immutable release records are authoritative; optional published tags must never be moved or substituted for local evidence. A failed gate blocks promotion, not further repair work.
mandates.title: Verified Local Release Gate

mandates.imperative: The merge gate is a verified native local run on the actual candidate integration tree against the current local integration head. Serialize publication and compare-and-swap the head so parallel agents cannot publish against stale proof. Conflicts, failed tests, missing evidence and stale source identities fail closed without losing work. Optional GitHub branch-push Test, auto-merge.yml and scripts/reconcile-prs.sh are publication adapters and cannot replace or become prerequisites for local development, debug releases, integration or production qualification. Future agents must repair gaps in the native gate rather than defer required verification to hosted CI.
mandates.title: Local Integrated-Tree Gate

mandates.imperative: Bare arguments are mission intent, and a mission spends inference money, boots the daemon and writes evidence — so input that is **shaped like a command** is refused before any of that happens. A flag-shaped argv (`susi release --help`) or a nested command word (`susi scan`) exits 2 with a did-you-mean (`susi admin release`, `susi ecosystem scan`) and writes nothing; only prose (several words, or a quoted sentence) becomes a mission. New commands are top-level or reachable by a path the guard can name, and `E2E_CHECKS` covers the refusal. Agents must not pass a command-shaped string to susi hoping it will be run.
mandates.title: Commands Are Not Missions

mandates.imperative: SUSI's brain is chosen **per task class from recorded outcomes**, not a hand-typed vendor order: every provider call records whether it answered and how fast, mission outcomes are folded back once per mission (`brain:*` receipts, non-citable), and providers are tried best-first for the prompt's class (`reflex`, `chat`, `code`, `reasoning`) with **local as the floor and cloud as the ceiling**. Privacy policy, budget ceilings and cooldowns are hard filters applied before ranking. **A failed or unfunded model can never be the brain**: no-credit and rejected-key failures quarantine the vendor's credential scope on a 10 min / 1 h / 6 h ladder, a provider with poor evidence and a recent failure sorts behind every healthy one even if it is the sticky preferred cloud, and the preference moves to a healthy cloud and returns when the original works. Keys are never removed or disabled by a failure — an operator can top up at any time. Cost is a tiered factor (`config/cost-tiers.json`, `SUSI_BUDGET=low|balanced|max`) that evidence outweighs. `susi brain` shows why.
mandates.title: Evidence-Ranked Brain

mandates.imperative: All Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) provider credentials stored in local memory or passed via multi-tenant ingress headers must enforce masked key previews and optional dollar-denominated spend ceilings (`max_budget_usd`). Spend accumulation is recorded atomically before inference dispatch, and credentials exceeding budget ceilings are automatically quarantined until cleared or topped up by the operator.
mandates.title: BYOK Key Governance & Spend Cap Isolation

mandates.imperative: The substrate enforces the Generalized Model Context Protocol (GMCP 2026 specification) across all tool, prompt, completion, resource, task, and server lifecycle interfaces. Tool poisoning, prompt injection, rug-pull, and data exfiltration defenses are evaluated before tool execution or session registration.
mandates.title: GMCP 2026 Protocol Conformance

mandates.imperative: `unsafe` is strictly forbidden or denied in every crate across the workspace. Substrate, transport, client, and library crates enforce `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`. Crates interfacing with OS-level FFI or hardware intrinsics enforce `#![deny(unsafe_code)]` with per-function `#[allow(unsafe_code)]` requiring a documented `// SAFETY:` justification. Panicking macros (`unwrap`, `expect`, `panic`, `todo`) are denied workspace-wide in production code. Native local verification must enforce these bounds; the existing CI Unsafe Exposure Ratchet remains supplementary coverage and is not a GitHub prerequisite.
mandates.title: Unsafe Code Ban & Auditable Safety Justifications

mandates.imperative: All `susi-*` crates declare zero direct third-party dependencies across normal, build, and dev targets. Every external crates.io or git crate is owned by exactly one `susi-vendor-*` crate, serving as an implementation vendor or pure re-export facade. Consumers import vendor capabilities exclusively through vendor facade paths (`use susi_vendor_*`), guaranteeing modular architectural isolation, clean dependency boundaries, and strict auditability.
mandates.title: Vendor Facade Isolation & Zero Direct Third-Party Dependencies

mandates.imperative: The Susi harness must own planning, scoped claims, isolated workers, model budgeting, verification, serialized local integration, release qualification and task closure. Existing native local-workflow and local-build commands are the available migration building blocks; do not describe missing integration or promotion as implemented. Run agents in parallel only with disjoint ownership and isolated writable state. Carry the CEO mandates into every delegated task via susi_core::self_build::BRIEF and canonical AGENTS.md pointers. GitHub and human engineering are not required stages. A missing harness capability is work for agents to implement and verify, not a reason to require CEO code inspection or weaken a gate.
mandates.title: Native Harness Owns the Complete Agent Loop

mandates.imperative: The CEO never looks at code. Agents own architecture, implementation, tests, debugging, dependency migration, conflict resolution, local integration and production qualification end-to-end. Communicate outcomes, measured evidence and genuine blockers in CEO language. Do not ask the CEO to inspect code or perform technical steps, and do not declare a partial foundation complete. Preserve explicit user authorization, privacy, spending and destructive-action boundaries. These mandates are requirements; current compliance must be demonstrated, not asserted.
mandates.title: CEO Vision and Agent-Only Delivery

mandates.imperative: Susi-authored runtime and development/distribution tooling must be Rust. Audit the full shipped dependency closure, build scripts, native objects and bundled helpers for each supported target/profile/feature set; required C/C++ and other-language implementation dependencies must be replaced. A Rust facade, optional-feature label or downloaded binary is not evidence of Rust-only compliance. Host OS ABI and toolchain boundaries must be inventoried explicitly and must not conceal bundled foreign runtimes. Preserve functionality and test it when replacing dependencies; do not satisfy purity by silently removing required local/cloud AI capabilities.
mandates.title: Complete Rust Dependency Closure

mandates.imperative: Windows installation, development, debug and production builds, tests, services, process management, paths and updates must use Windows-native interfaces and the native MSVC Rust target. No Bash, WSL, MSYS, Python, Node, Unix emulation or container prerequisite may exist on the compliant path. Exercise clean-machine setup, drive/UNC paths, Unicode paths, reserved names, junctions, file locking and atomic promotion. Record actual Windows artifacts and tests; cross-compilation or source inspection alone does not prove Windows-native operation.
mandates.title: Native Windows as a First-Class Platform

mandates.imperative: Schedule independent tasks concurrently in isolated worktrees/branches with unique identities, private target outputs, runtime homes, ports and task scopes. Enforce scope ownership, serialize integration, revalidate the combined tree, and preserve changes on conflict or crash. Share only safe immutable dependency/toolchain caches with explicit validation. Measure cold/warm build time, queue contention, concurrent throughput and resource use; blazing-fast is a performance objective, never an unmeasured claim. Do not oversubscribe the host or remove correctness gates to improve reported speed.
mandates.title: Measured Parallelism Without Shared-State Conflicts

mandates.imperative: Planning, claiming, implementing, committing, testing, integrating, debug builds and production qualification must complete locally without GitHub accounts, API calls, Actions, pull requests or remote claim refs. Local Git is permitted; optional repository hosting and publication cannot determine local correctness. Vendor or provision reproducible sources and record their provenance; offline mode must account for build-script downloads as well as Cargo resolution. A cold machine may need explicit toolchain/dependency provisioning, which must be documented and tested rather than hidden behind a warm cache.
mandates.title: GitHub-Independent Local Development

mandates.imperative: Provide distinct native debug and optimized production artifacts. Debug instances never overwrite production. Qualify the exact candidate with tests, policy checks, executable smoke tests, digest and provenance before atomic promotion; retain the previous verified artifact, check health and roll back on failure. Test promotion and rollback, including interruption and file-lock behavior on Windows. Agents own these steps. No compile-only result, scope receipt, version string, hosted tag or documentation statement is a release attestation.
mandates.title: Separate Debug and Production With Atomic Promotion

mandates.imperative: Susi and the distributed ecosystem may use only Apache-2.0, MIT, BSD-2-Clause or BSD-3-Clause license grants. Evaluate complete SPDX expressions correctly: AND obligations must all comply; an allowed OR branch must actually be available; additional exceptions and other licenses are not silently accepted. Audit code, transitive dependencies, build/runtime helpers, model weights, tokenizer assets and bundled data as applicable. Preserve upstream notices and attribution. Replace or remove incompatible components legitimately; never relabel third-party code, delete license obligations, exclude a shipped dependency from the audit or broaden the allowlist to manufacture success. Inventory platform/toolchain services separately; that boundary is not a license loophole for distributed components. Record external protocol-peer and service licenses accurately; connecting to them neither relicenses them nor certifies their policy compliance.
mandates.title: Apache BSD MIT License Closure Only

mandates.imperative: Remove unused dependencies, dead paths, duplicate implementations, unnecessary default features, oversized mandatory services and speculative frameworks. Every shipped capability needs an owner, purpose and evidence. Track executable/distribution size, idle memory, startup, latency and cold/warm build costs with repeatable budgets; regressions require measured justification and must not be hidden by a narrower audit. Preserve necessary functionality when replacing dependencies. Zero bloat is a continuing acceptance discipline, not proof that every remaining byte is indispensable.
mandates.title: Zero Bloat Through Measured Budgets

mandates.imperative: The normal local and cloud Susi experience must discover host capabilities and select safe operating defaults without user-written config files, environment tuning, port selection or technical repair steps. Agents own setup, provisioning diagnosis and recovery. Test clean-machine and upgrade paths and preserve deliberate user choices. Credentials, privacy consent, paid-service authorization and spending caps remain explicit; zero configuration never means inventing credentials, making purchases or bypassing consent. Missing permissions or services must be reported honestly and cannot masquerade as successful setup.
mandates.title: Zero Required User Configuration

mandates.imperative: The product proposition is Susi: AI that earns its next upgrade. Autonomous improvements must carry reproducible evidence linking the goal, prior baseline, candidate source/dependencies/toolchain, correctness tests, resource measurements and actual integrated artifact. Promote only demonstrated improvement without forbidden regressions and retain a verified rollback path. Persist and retrieve learning evidence durably; generating an embedding alone is not permanent memory. Models cannot certify their own success. The proposition is an engineering acceptance requirement, not an unsupported market-uniqueness or completed recursive-self-improvement claim.
mandates.title: Susi Earns Every Upgrade

protocols.imperative: Each agent has a private worktree, target directory and runtime scratch home; writable artifacts and ports are never shared. Preserve production state and other workers. Mandates 49, 52 and 65 define verification.
protocols.title: Workspace Purity

protocols.imperative: Build and execution must maximize hardware utilization without exceeding physical limits.
protocols.title: Hardware Saturation

protocols.imperative: Native local release sequence: identify clean candidate and locked dependency graph -> strict license and Rust-only audits -> formatting/clippy/nonempty tests -> build and smoke-test the actual executable in isolated state -> record artifact digest and source/toolchain/target provenance -> atomic promotion -> health check -> rollback on failure. Every step gates the next. GitHub publication is optional and follows qualification. Mandates 53, 67 and 71 govern; do not confuse this release sequence with Mandate 20 architecture/implementation order.
protocols.title: Motion Rule (Release Gate)

protocols.imperative: Mandatory use of conventional commit prefixes and zero-emoji policy.
protocols.title: Conventional Reflex

protocols.imperative: Prioritize pre-compiled binary deployment with transparent local build fallback (Mandate 47 one-line install surface).
protocols.title: Binary Dominance

protocols.imperative: Installer must inject `.susi/bin` into host environment variables (Mandate 47).
protocols.title: Auto-Path Injection

protocols.imperative: A single compiled binary deployed at `~/.susi/bin/susi` (the host-contract path; Mandate 47). Invocations in `cwd` capture local workspace context, check `~/.susi/substrate.lock`, and ensure `global susi` owns ports/models without duplicate daemons. Detecting binary signature changes (`binary.hash`), `susi` evicts the stale daemon and hot-reloads `global susi` from the canonical binary automatically. The canonical binary is written only by the installer (Mandate 47) or by release promotion (Mandate 48). Dev builds never write it; they run as their own instance.
protocols.title: Canonical Binary Dynamics & Hot-Reload Protocol

steps.imperative: Non-blocking asynchronous listener stages intents in the lock-free `SubstratePulseQueue`.
steps.title: Pulse Ingestion

steps.imperative: GAWD constructs a Dynamic Execution Graph (DAG), recruiting specialists via `NeuralAgentFactory`.
steps.title: Swarm Synthesis

steps.imperative: Swarm outputs pass `TruthTransformer` absolute-evidence gates (live `EvidenceSession` citations, compiled binary reads, or native verified receipts). Soft model review is not a completion path.
steps.title: Truth Convergence

steps.imperative:
- **`global susi` Primes `AlphaSelf`**: The background daemon profiles host hardware/OS, provisions model ladder weights, owns host-contract ports 9090–9094, and maintains global evidence ledgers.
- **`susi` Primes `AlphaWorld`**: Unconditionally jailed to `cwd`, `susi` indexes local project files, runs unit test audits, and applies workspace changes through transactional patch cycles (`susi tx`).
- **`susi` Primes `susi repo`**: When `cwd` is the engine's source code, `susi` engages self-evolution, running tests, syncing version manifests (`susi admin sync`), and qualifying and promoting verified artifacts through Mandates 53, 67 and 71.
